Table S7 Compound information, efficacy labels and model evaluation on the PTNC
dataset

A. Information on the 81 compounds included in the PTNC dataset. Compounds were
indexed by their corresponding Pert_IDs and were purchased from TargetMol. The table
includes compound name, catalog number, CAS number, SMILES, molecular formula,
pathway annotations, indication, solvent, target annotations and drug type.

 B. This table summarizes the cell viability assays used to determine compound efficacy based
on the 24 h response. Each cell viability assay was performed with three biological replicates.
Drug responses were labelled as resistant (N; negative class) or sensitive (Y; positive class)
according to the efficacy criteria described in the Methods. Cell-line-compound combinations
with inconsistent labels across repeated experiments were removed; therefore, the resulting
compound-by-cell-line matrix is not fully orthogonal.

evidence.title: S8 PTPC legend
evidence.text:
Table S8 Sample metadata, compound information and proteomic profiles for PTPC.

A. Sample-level metadata for the PTPC dataset, an independent perturbation proteomics
dataset generated across five cancer cell lines (A375, HCT116, NCI-H1975, NCI-H2170 and
Panc 10.05). Proteomic profiles were collected at 6 h and 24 h after treatment, with control
samples assigned a perturbation time of 0 h. This table lists 2217 non-pooled samples,
comprising 2021 independent proteomic samples and 196 technical or biological replicates.
The 90 pooled samples are included in the total PTPC sample count but are not listed in this
table. After accounting for pooled and replicate samples, PTPC contained 2021 independent
proteomic samples for model evaluation.

B. Compound information for the 716 perturbation identifiers used in PTPC, corresponding to
708 unique compound names. All compounds were purchased from TargetMol. Information
includes perturbation ID, catalog number, compound name, CAS number, SMILES,
molecular formula, pathway annotations, indication, solvent, target annotations and
compound type.

C. Matched protein abundance matrix for the same 2217 non-pooled sample records. Rows
correspond to samples and columns correspond to quantified proteins annotated by UniProt
accession and and gene name concatenated with an underscore (e.g.,
A0A1B0GUA7_TEX51).

evidence.title: Supplementary dose response method
evidence.text:
Dose-response curve fitting and IC comparison
Luminescence values were normalized to the untreated control wells and used to calculate
relative cell viability. For curve fitting, viability values were first converted to relative
inhibition by subtracting them from one, and the transformed values were constrained to the
range of 0 to 1 to reduce the impact of out-of-range measurements caused by experimental
variability. Dose-response curves were fitted using a sigmoidal model, and IC values were
estimated from the fitted curves. The fitted values from this model were used for the main
dose-response plots and IC estimation in Figures 5G-I. For each concentration, three
independent biological replicates were collected and processed in the same manner; these
replicate-level values are shown overlaid on the fitted curves in SI Figure 4. Statistical
comparisons between cisplatin (M0) and each compound (M1) were performed using
likelihood-ratio tests based on the fitted models. The deviance was calculated as
D=2 � (logLikM1 - logLikM0). The resulting deviance was compared with a chi-squared
distribution, with degrees of freedom equal to the difference in the number of fitted
parameters. A P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
